seo.meta_title: What Does 잡아떼다 Mean? | Flatly Denying Something in Korean
seo.meta_description: AI translates 잡아떼다 as 'grab and tear off'. It means flatly denying something you clearly did. Learn 잡아떼다 and 시치미를 떼다.

ai_failure.situation: Your Korean friend complains about her younger brother: 내 과자 먹고 끝까지 아니라고 잡아떼.
ai_failure.ai_mistake: Translates 잡아떼 as 'grabs and tears off'.
ai_failure.why_it_fails: 잡아떼다 means insisting you didn't do something when you clearly did — denying it to someone's face. It's always said about someone else, with frustration or amusement.

natural_solution.rule: 잡아떼다 = flatly deny, play innocent. Often with 모른다고 or 아니라고. Its twin idiom is 시치미를 떼다.

alternatives.context: 'He flatly said he didn't know anything'
Neutral, formal: 'He denied it to the end' — the word used in news

nuance: Both 잡아떼다 and 시치미를 떼다 use 떼다 ('take off'). 시치미 was the name tag tied to a hunting falcon; removing it hid whose bird it was. So 'taking off the tag' became pretending you have nothing to do with something. Kids, partners and politicians are the usual subjects.
